G0 polarimetric model for PolSAR data (R6)

Source: R/models.R
G0Polarimetric.Rd

R6 class for the \(\mathcal{G}^0_m(\alpha, \Sigma, L)\) law (see dg0p()). Following Nascimento, Ferreira and Frery (2023), \(\Sigma\) is estimated by the sample mean (since \(E(Z) = \Sigma\)) and \((\alpha, L)\) by maximising the likelihood (analytic score). The variance of the entropy estimator combines the inverse observed information of \((\alpha, L)\) with a moment estimate of the variance of \(m\log|\hat\Sigma|\).

Examples

set.seed(1)
Z <- rg0p(400, alpha = -4, Sigma = polsar_example_sigma("urban"), L = 4)
m <- G0Polarimetric$new()$fit(Z, L = 4)
m
#> <G0 polarimetric> fitted to n = 400 observations
#>   alpha = -4.56299
#>   Sigma:
#>                   [,1]              [,2]             [,3]
#> [1,]  0.88150+0.00000i  0.02508+0.00207i -0.15380+0.1836i
#> [2,]  0.02508-0.00207i  0.05535+0.00000i -0.00867+0.0141i
#> [3,] -0.15380-0.18360i -0.00867-0.01410i  0.47100+0.0000i
#>   L = 4 (fixed)
#>   logLik = 3778.55
#>   Shannon entropy = -9.51015
m$entropy_variance()
#> [1] 0.0976793
